children: , the flash-memory and data-storage producer, slid approximately 3.5% to $1,632.67 Friday, even after Oracle delivered 121% cloud-infrastructure growth. That contradiction defined the week: AI data centers kept consuming storage, memory supplies remained tight, and investors still sold the shares.

The operating numbers remain fierce. SanDisk's fiscal fourth-quarter revenue hit $8.97 billion, jumping 51% sequentially and 372% year over year, according to its earnings coverage. Management projected $10.3 billion to $10.8 billion for the following quarter after securing ten major customer supply agreements in six months. But pricingnot shipment volumegenerated roughly two-thirds of the latest sequential growth, making future gains increasingly dependent on sustained memory scarcity.

The $10.55 billion guidance midpoint points to another 17.6% sequential revenue increase, but SanDisk's market value has already ballooned to approximately $256 billion. The chart captures that tension: excellent growth and financial strength are offset by almost nonexistent GF Value and Momentum readings, leaving the GF Score at just 51 out of 100. Oracle's results strengthen the AI-storage demand thesis, yet Friday's retreat suggests SanDisk's valuation now demands relentless pricing power with almost no room for disappointment.

title: SanDisk Drops Over 3% as Oracle's AI Boom Fails to Lift Memory
